: 
This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation .
2.

The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 08.05.2017 at about 8.40 a.m. while moving on motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA04JD1123 as a pillion rider on left side of the road, rider of the said motor cycle had parked at median with view to cross the SCCH 5 road with indicator in a signal near Adithya College, Yelahanka, meantime auto bearing Reg.No.KA04AC 8782 came in high speed rash and negligently, endangering to human life from opposite direction and taken right turn coming to the extreme right side without indication or signal and dashed against petitioner's vehicle,
due to the impact of the said accident, petitioner fell down and sustained multiple fracture like displaced fracture of shaft of both tibia and fibula of left leg.

Immediately he was shifted to Maruthi Hospital, wherein he has taken treatment, thereafter shifted to Bowring Hospital, surgery is conducted, implant is fixed on his left leg, for all he has spent an amount of Rs.1,00,000/.

3. At the time of the accident, he was aged about 21 years old, he was a student and parttime worker,
drawing monthly salary of Rs.12,000/ p.m., he was sole SCCH 5 earner of his family, because of the this accident, he has lost his earnings and bread.
Out of this accident crime No.268/2017 is registered against the said auto and its driver before Yelahanka Traffic Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.
R1 is the insurer, R2 is owner of the said auto, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.20,00,000/.
4.

On service of notice, respondent No.1/insurer has appeared and filed written statement denying entire case of the petitioner, further stated that, petitioner has to prove all the allegations about accident, injury and medical expenses, further he has to prove his age and income, further there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act, he is entitled to take shelter under SCCH 5 Sec.170 of M.V.Act, rider of the motor cycle had no driving license at the time of accident, further driver of the auto also had no driving license at the time of accident, owner of the auto/R2 has to comply the policy conditions, claim made by the petitioner is higher side, hence petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. On service of notice, R2/owner has not appeared before the court, hence placed exparte.

6. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, on 08.05.2017 at about 8.40 a.m. while he was proceeding as a pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA04 JD1123 and Sri. Pruthviraj H.P vs Sriram General Insurance on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145116658/
2

sentences.text: waiting to cross the road near Kogilu Main Road, Bengaluru, at SCCH 5 that time, a driver of the auto bearing Reg.No.KA04AC8782 driven in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle, as a result of which petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?

If so from which respondent?
3. What order or award?
7. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW1, examined 2 witnesses as PW2 and PW3, marked 16 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, counsel for R1 submitted that, he has no defence evidence, accordingly evidence is closed.
SCCH 5 8.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1:

As per the case of the petitioner, very accident is occurred at Kogilu main road, at about 8.40 a.m. on 08.05.2017 due to negligency of driver of the auto bearing Reg.No.KA04AC 8782 while moving on motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA04JD1123 as a pillion rider, but auto driver is not a party to this petition, owner of the auto is made as party to this petition as R2, he has not appeared and contested the petition inspIte of service of notice against him.

R1/insurer has appeared and filed SCCH 5 objection, wherein he has not denied place, date and time of the accident, but he has denied negligency of the auto driver and stated that very accident is occurred due to negligency of the motor cyclist.
10.
In chiefexamination petitioner has deposed that, without giving signal, auto driver has taken the auto on immediate right, so that, this accident is caused.
In crossexamination also he has reiterated the said facts and there is no such admissions.

Further it is noticed that as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.7 i.e., police papers it is noticed that, charge sheet is only against the driver of the auto by name Venkatesh, but not against the rider of the motor cycle.
Further there are medial records about taking of treatment with regard to cause of the accident.

11. On the other hand, counsel for R1 denied the case of the petitioner by way of crossexamination,

3 but SCCH 5 not given defence evidence.

sentences.text: Under such circumstances, this tribunal is of the opinion that, the evidence given by the petitioner is sufficient to hold that, on the alleged place, date and time this accident is occurred only due to negligency of auto driver and said fact is proved by the petitioner.
Hence I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained displaced fracture of shaft of tibia and fibula left leg.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.5.
13.

Insupport of case of he petitioner, Medical Record Technician at Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital has examined as PW2 and furnished authorization letter marked as Ex.P.10, copy of Police Intimation marked as Ex.P.11, copy of MLC register is marked as Ex.P.12, case SCCH 5 sheet marked as Ex.P.13 and Xray Films marked as Ex.P.14.
Further Dr.S.A.Somashekar is examined as PW3 wherein he has specifically deposed that, there is displaced fracture of shaft of tibia and fibula left leg and surgery is conducted.

As per his version there is disability at the rate of 35% to left lower limb and after conversion whole body disability at the rate of 17%.
14.
In this regard, he has relied upon OPD card marked as Ex.P.15, Xray Films marked as Ex.P.16.
In crossexamination admits that, petitioner has not taken treatment in their hospital and he has not treated the petitioner.

There is no infection, there was fracture of bot bones of left leg, which may take 46 months for recovery, he do not know about follow up treatment, he ha assessed only physical disability, as per his knowledge petitioner was working as coolie and taken treatment in SCCH 5 Government hospital, they used to issue bill at the rate of 50%.

15. Further admits that, bill may be only for an amount of Rs.1,836/, further denied that, at the ost disability to the lower limb will come at the rate of 20% and whole body disability at the rate of will come at the rate of 7%.
further admitted that, accident is occurred in the year 2017 and he has assessed disability in the year 2022.

16. On going through the evidence of the Doctor it is noticed that, as per his version, disability to the particular limb is at the rate of 35%, whole body disability at the rate of is at the rate of 17%, but it is noticed that he has not treated the petitioner, not issued disability certificate, only he has assessed disability.

Further as per the case of the petitioner, he is coolie, but SCCH 5 nature of work is not mentioned, treatment is given at Bowring hospital, medical bills are only for Rs.1,836/ which are marked as Ex.P.8, discharge summary is not furnished.

On going through the medical records it is noticed that, petitioner has taken treatment as indoor patient since 08.05.2017 to 13.05.2017, there are both bone fracture in left leg tibia and fibula and which are united, hence disability is considered at the rate of 30% to particular limb and after converting to whole body, whole body disability at the rate of 10%, accordingly disability is considered at the rate of 10% for the purpose of calculation of future income.
17.

As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 21 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked which is not marked, on perusal of the same he is born on 05.06.1997 and the SCCH 5 alleged accident is occurred on 08.05.2017, accordingly his age is considered about 20 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 18 is applicable with Sri. sentences.text: 18. As per his case, he was student cum part time worker and drawing salary of Rs.12,000/ p.m. to prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.11,000/ p.m.

sentences.text:
Keeping in mind injuries caused to the petitioner, treatment taken, expenses incurred and also the pain suffered, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just and necessary to allot compensation under other heads, accordingly for pain and sufferings compensation of Rs.15,000/
is awarded, for conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges Rs.15,000/ is awarded, for loss of amenities of life Rs.15,000/ is awarded, further he is entitled for Rs.11,000/ towards loss of income during laid up period.

Further petitioner is also entitled for compensation for medical expenses incurred by him, for which, he has produced medical bills marked as Ex.P.8 for an amount of Rs.1,836/.
20.

Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below: SCCH 5 Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1.
Loss of future income 2,37,60000 2.
Pain and sufferings 15,00000 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,00000 attendant charges 4.
Medical Expenses 1,836 00 5.
Loss of amenities in life 15,00000 6.
Loss of income during laid up 11,00000 period Total 2,95,43600 21.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,95,436/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

22. In the case on hand, respondent No.1 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.418005/31/18/000479, which is valid for the period from 18.04.2017 to 17.04.2018, the alleged accident was occurred on 08.05.2017, it reveals that, as on the date of SCCH 5 accident insurance policy was in force.
Further driver of the auto had driving licence at the time of the accident, hence naturally liability shall go against R1, so that, R1/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount Sri.

23. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,95,436/ (Rupees Two Lakhs Ninety Five Thousand Four Hundred Thirty Six Only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
SCCH 5 The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through epayment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
